question: Explain how Mencius achieves multi-leader high throughput by partitioning the Paxos instance space, and how it skips empty instances using SKIP messages.
Describe how Raft's Pre-Vote phase prevents disrupted partitioned nodes from causing leadership instability upon network reconnection.
In distributed systems, what is the Byzantine Generals Problem under synchronous vs asynchronous networks? State the FLP Impossibility connection.
Explain how PN-Counter (Positive-Negative Counter) CRDT works by combining two G-Counters (Grow-Only Counters) for increments and decrements.
Describe how Google Spanner uses TrueTime API with GPS and atomic clocks to achieve external consistency without wide-area lock synchronization.
Explain how Chubby lock service uses coarse-grained distributed locking with Paxos to prevent split-brain in master-worker architectures.
Explain the Raft log invariance proof: why cannot a leader commit a log entry from an older term by simply counting replicas?
Analyze how HotStuff consensus simplifies PBFT view change complexity from O(n^2) to linear O(n) using threshold signatures and a Pacemaker.
Explain how distributed transaction saga pattern maintains eventual data consistency using compensating transactions instead of 2PC locks.
Describe how dynamic quorum reconfiguration via vertical Paxos decouples consensus from state machine execution.
Explain how Lookup Arguments in Plookup use sorting and grand products to prove values exist in a precomputed table in O(n log n) time.
Detail the role of elliptic curve endomorphisms and GLV method in accelerating scalar multiplication in cryptographic provers.
Explain how zero-knowledge SNARKs achieve zero-knowledge by blinding witness polynomials with random polynomial multiples of the vanishing polynomial.
Explain how Nova achieves incrementally verifiable computation (IVC) using relaxed R1CS folding without expensive FFTs or trusted setups.
Explain the mechanics of Pedersen Hash functions on Edwards curves and why they are efficient inside SNARK circuits.
Describe how multivariate polynomial commitments (like Multilinear KZG or Hyrax) avoid FFT interpolation in high-degree circuits.
Explain the difference between knowledge soundness and standard soundness in interactive proof systems.
Explain how recursive SNARK proofs aggregate thousands of transaction proofs into a single constant-sized on-chain validity proof.
Describe the role of quotient polynomial degree in Groth16 and why the SRS degree d must equal the number of multiplication gates m.
Explain how Plonky2 combines STARK-like FRI commitments with small 64-bit Goldilocks field to achieve sub-second proof generation.
Explain the Color Code on a 2D triangular/hexagonal lattice and why all Clifford gates can be implemented transversally on color codes.
Describe how Floquet quantum error-correcting codes (such as the Honeycomb code) dynamically cycle measurements without static stabilizers.
Explain how coherent noise (unitary rotation drift) accumulates quadratically in quantum circuits compared to stochastic Pauli noise.
Describe how quantum error detection differs from error correction, and how [[4, 2, 2]] detects single-qubit errors without correcting them.
Explain how catastrophic cosmic ray or phonon burst events cause correlated multi-qubit errors across planar superconducting chips.
Describe the role of boundary rough edges and smooth edges in encoding logical |0_L> and |+_L> states in surface codes.
Explain how randomized benchmarking (RB) measures average Clifford gate fidelity independently of state preparation and measurement (SPAM) errors.
Explain how bosonic quantum codes (such as GKP codes - Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill) protect information within infinite-dimensional continuous oscillator spaces.
Describe how the Knill-Laflamme conditions state the necessary and sufficient algebraic criteria for quantum error correction.
Explain the concept of quantum LDPC codes with non-zero asymptotic code rate [[n, kn, dn]] overcoming 2D planar geometric limits.
Explain how symplectic integrators preserve Poincaré invariants in multi-degree-of-freedom Hamiltonian systems.
Explain the role of Monomial Symplectic maps and generating functions in preserving canonical phase space geometry.
Describe how implicit midpoint rule achieves unconditional symplecticity for non-separable Hamiltonian neural networks.
Explain how continuous-depth neural networks avoid shattered gradient phenomena that plague ultra-deep feedforward networks.
Describe how Neural Jump SDEs combine continuous drift-diffusion with discrete Poisson jump processes for irregular event modelling.
Explain how Riemannian Neural ODEs generalize continuous flow networks to curved manifolds (such as spheres and hyperbolic spaces).
Describe how symplectic shadow Hamiltonians prevent secular drift in long-term orbital predictions of astronomical systems.
Explain the role of Barbalat's Lemma in proving asymptotic stability of continuous-time adaptive neural controllers.
Explain how Hamiltonian Generative Adversarial Networks (H-GANs) eliminate mode collapse by preserving phase space volume.
Analyze the connection between optimal transport, Wasserstein distance, and continuous normalizing flows under Benamou-Brenier formulation.
Explain how Slice Categories C/A and Coslice Categories A/C model generalized objects equipped with a morphism to/from a fixed base object.
Explain the universal property of Equalizers and Coequalizers in category theory and how they formalize equation solutions.
Describe how Pullbacks and Pushouts generalize fibred products and fibred coproducts in category theory.
Explain how Kan Extensions (Left Kan Extension Lan_K F and Right Kan Extension Ran_K F) universalize all categorical concepts.
Describe the role of Monads in modeling stateful imperative computation in Haskell (IO and State monads).
Explain how Enriched Category Theory replaces Hom-sets with objects in an arbitrary monoidal category V.
Describe the Beck-Chevalley condition in categorical logic and how it formalizes substitution commuting with quantifiers.
Explain how Lawvere Theories provide a purely categorical formulation of universal algebra without variable binding.
Explain how Operads generalize categories to multi-input operations (trees and string diagrams).
Explain how Higher Category Theory (infinity-categories and quasicategories) models homotopy theory where morphisms are defined up to coherent higher homotopies.
